objective: A frozen census of the 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws read over abstract names as count laws of degree four: for each, the pairs (value, number of 1-neighbours) that occur, the values and value pairs on edges, the joint states of one neighbour distinction and its two endpoint values over all allowed states, and their K1-K3 verdict by knotlab (the two values as loops' distinctions, the neighbour distinction as the contact); for one law of each knot shape, target 5's switch and swaps carried out on an explicit board. Predictions C1 (no law undecided), C2 (a knot exactly when both values occur and some value pair never shares an edge) and C3 (the moves succeed for every shape).
status: Closed: supported 2026-11-10 (frozen, exact; C1, C2 and C3 held): of the 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws read over abstract names as count laws of degree four, 31 have no state; in 90 of the other 993 one neighbour distinction and its two endpoint values form a knot by knotlab's K1-K3 (29 never put two 0s side by side, 29 never two 1s, 31 never a 0 beside a 1, 1 only a 0 beside a 1), exactly when both values occur and some pair never shares an edge (C2); the switch and both exchanges succeed for the three shapes with a connected two-valued frozen board (C3), while the shape with no mixed edge has none and is covered by ticket A's T5 on two monochromatic boards.
